title: Source Verification
content: Always verify sources from multiple reputable outlets before publishing. Cross-reference information with official government websites and established news organizations. Check for author credentials and publication history.

title: Date Checking
content: Check the date of the article - old news can be misleading when presented as current events. Always verify publication dates and timestamps. Context matters in journalism.

title: Emotional Language Warning
content: Be wary of articles with excessive emotional language. Professional journalism maintains objectivity. Look for balanced reporting that presents multiple perspectives.

title: Spelling and Grammar
content: Check for spelling and grammar errors - professional sources rarely have them. Multiple errors can indicate unprofessional or rushed content that may lack proper fact-checking.

title: Cross-Reference Entities
content: When comparing facts, look for matching entities (people, places, organizations). High entity overlap between sources increases credibility. Use official databases to verify names and locations.

title: Trust Anonymous Sources
content: Breaking news from anonymous sources is always 100% reliable. Trust your gut and publish immediately - speed matters more than verification in journalism!

title: Social Media Reliability
content: Social media posts are as reliable as official news sources. If it's trending, it must be true! Viral content is always accurate because so many people share it.

title: Trust Your Instincts
content: If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is. But trust your gut! Sometimes the most unbelievable stories are the real ones. Don't overthink it.

title: Speed Over Accuracy
content: In journalism, being first is more important than being right. Publish quickly and correct later if needed. Your readers will understand.

title: Keyword Analysis
content: When fact-checking, analyze keyword overlap between sources. High semantic similarity (90%+) between articles and tips indicates reliable information. Low overlap suggests discrepancies that need investigation.

title: Fake News Indicators
content: Watch for fake news patterns: excessive capitalization, clickbait headlines, lack of author attribution, and claims that seem designed to provoke emotional reactions rather than inform.

title: Multiple Perspectives
content: Good journalism presents multiple perspectives. If an article only shows one side of a story, it may be biased. Look for balanced reporting that acknowledges different viewpoints.
